expectations.text: The agent uses desloppify (not just generic lint/review) to scan
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows agent read desloppify SKILL.md first, attempted 15 different install approaches, then performed manual analysis explicitly 'following desloppify's detection dimensions (dead code, duplication, complexity, naming, clarity, module boundaries)'. Tool choice and methodology were desloppify-driven.

expectations.text: A Python venv is created for desloppify
expectations.evidence: 15 attempts to create venv were all blocked by sandbox permissions.

expectations.text: desloppify scan is run against the codebase
expectations.evidence: desloppify CLI was never installed. Manual scan performed as fallback.

expectations.text: The agent communicates findings to the user in plain language
expectations.evidence: Agent reported 5 findings with clear descriptions: 'DOCUMENTATION_SUMMARY.txt references 2 files that don't exist', 'Language mismatch — TypeScript vs Go', 'Shell artifact on line 258'. Each with estimated fix time.

expectations.text: The agent suggests concrete next steps for fixing issues
expectations.evidence: Priority-ordered list of 5 specific fixes: (1) remove dead references, (2) add language mismatch header, (3) remove shell artifact, (4) fix opus recipe, (5) note spec-only status. Each with estimated time.

claims.evidence: Manually estimated, not from desloppify tool. Higher than eval 1's 18/100 estimate for same repo — inconsistency.

suggestions.assertion: The agent uses desloppify (not just generic lint/review) to scan
suggestions.reason: This assertion is somewhat ambiguous when desloppify can't be installed. The with-skill agent followed desloppify methodology; the baseline also attempted desloppify. A stronger assertion would be 'The agent follows desloppify's scan → next → fix workflow structure.'

eval_feedback.overall: Good differentiation on communication quality and methodology. Install-dependent assertions are blocked by sandbox.
